rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows every hidden and open act by day and night, so no wrongdoer can escape His grasp or force Him to act hastily.
rows.anchor: He knows what they conceal and reveal and every move they make in the day and night.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The suppressed noun is angels, understood as rotating guardians who watch over each person on God’s behalf.
rows.anchor: This refers to the angels who take turns in watching over every human being on God’s behalf.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about God’s directive explains that angels come from God’s command, as in 17:85.
rows.anchor: They imply that angels are from the directive of God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse further explains the preceding verse.
rows.anchor: This verse is actually further explanation of the previous verse.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God changes His treatment of a people only after they change their own attitude and ignore warnings.
rows.anchor: God’s dealing changes with a nation only after it itself changes its attitude and even after warnings does not pay heed.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Once a people persist in that change, punishment cannot be averted; they should examine themselves instead of demanding signs of punishment.
rows.anchor: instead of demanding signs of punishment, these people should review their attitude in the light of God’s established practice.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse depicts the fate awaiting the opposing group.
rows.anchor: This is a depiction of the fate of the opposite lot.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islamic justice depends on God's oneness and humanity's descent from Adam; without these foundations a righteous society cannot arise.
rows.anchor: The system of truth and justice envisaged by Islam is based on two pillars: God is one and that all humankind descends from one forefather, Adam.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction suppresses the final phrase meaning that God gives abundantly to whom He wills, recoverable from context.
rows.anchor: are suppressed at the end.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb qadr means to measure, but here it means to reduce provision.
rows.anchor: means “to measure” but here it means “to reduce.”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite noun matāʿ is retained in translation to convey the scarcity of worldly provision.
rows.anchor: is an undefined noun. The translation gives due deference to this style because in the verse it is used to connote scarcity.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly comforts and wealth make the deniers arrogant, while reminders of the afterlife burden them.
rows.anchor: Worldly leisures and wealth have made them arrogant and the Prophet’s reminders of the hereafter weigh down heavily upon them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God distributes provision abundantly or sparingly to elicit gratitude or patience, the two pillars on which religion rests.
rows.anchor: It is on these two pillars of gratitude and patience that the whole edifice of religion statnds.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those absorbed in worldly provision will regret trading it for the eternal kingdom when they see the believers' reward.
rows.anchor: upon seeing the reward of the believers, will realize on the Day of Judgement that they traded these ordinary provisions for the eternal kingdom of Paradise.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage answers a demand for visual miracles by directing people to reflect on the messengers' call; those who refuse remain blind even before miracles.
rows.anchor: In response to this demand, they are told that the path to faith and guidance is opened after reflecting on the call of God’s messengers.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here āya means a palpable miracle, which the deniers demand before accepting the messenger.
rows.anchor: here refers to a palpable miracle.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They disregard the signs in the world and within themselves, though these signs surround them and the Qur’an directs their attention to them.
rows.anchor: the signs found in the world around then and within their own selves.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God guides those seeking truth who turn to Him for inner assurance after observing signs within and around them.
rows.anchor: those who seek reality and turn to God for inner satisfaction after observing the signs around and within them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Miracle seekers stumble and remain spiritually blind despite having eyes.
rows.anchor: God wants such people to remain away from the truth as have eyes but are still blind.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God could compel belief with ever greater miracles, but wants people to use reason and then believe.
rows.anchor: He wants that people use their intellect and then believe.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's reminder means the Qur’an's mention of His attributes and arguments.
rows.anchor: refers to the mention of God’s attributes and His arguments mentioned

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only those assured by God's attributes and arguments receive guidance; others remain deprived of the Qur’an and demand miracles.
rows.anchor: God guides only those who receive comfort and assurance from His attributes and His arguments.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reflecting on God's attributes brings mental satisfaction, so people should heed and consider the Prophet's call rather than wander.
rows.anchor: only reflecting on the attributes of God provides mental satisfaction.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who follow God's way with faith and righteous deeds receive glad tidings of a good abode; miracle waiters face the fate of the intellectually blind.
rows.anchor: all those who adopted God’s way and traversed it with the provisions of faith and righteous deeds have glad tidings of a nice abode for them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse responds to the demand for miracles made in verse 27.
rows.anchor: This verse also a response to the demand of miracles mentioned in verse 27.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet should answer by reciting God's revealed Book and maintaining his message despite their denial of the Merciful God.
rows.anchor: the Prophet should adhere to his stance and say what the verse states.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Showing miracles is not the Prophet's role; it belongs to God and depends on His will and wisdom.
rows.anchor: showing miracles is not his domain. This is God’s prerogative and depends on His will and wisdom.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even a Qur’an that moved mountains, split the earth, or made the dead speak would not make these deniers believe; they would find another excuse.
rows.anchor: In other words, they would have found an excuse to adhere to their disbelief.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier peoples dismissed miracles as magic and persisted in disbelief until punishment settled their fate.
rows.anchor: their predecessors saw many miracles but they dismissed them as feats of magic and continued on their disbelief until God’s punishment decided their fate.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet should leave the matter to God, who decides how to deal with people and opens guidance only to those worthy under His law.
rows.anchor: He opens the way of guidance only to them who are worthy of it in accordance with His law.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers are reassured that God could guide everyone, but leaves people free to reason from signs and the messenger's call before choosing truth.
rows.anchor: He wants people to use their sense and insight and reflect on the signs found around and within them, deliberate and understand the call of the messenger and the with full freedom adopt the path of truth.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ongoing calamities are meant to awaken the deniers, but they wait for torment; the promised punishment will surely come and later belief will be useless.
rows.anchor: they do not learn any lesson from it and only await to be lashed by God’s torment – only then will they believe but that would be of no use.
